knowledge:
- key_parameters: adducts=Character vector of expected adducts (e.g., c("[M+H]+", "[M+Na]+")) used to calculate m/z values from exact masses ;; tolerance=Absolute m/z tolerance for matching ;; ppm=Relative m/z tolerance (in parts-per-million) for matching ;; toleranceRt=Maximal acceptable absolute difference in retention times ;; rtColname=Name of the column containing retention times in the query and target datasets (defaults to "rt") ;; mzColname=Character vector of length 2 specifying the m/z column names in query and target datasets ;; requirePrecursor=Logical, if TRUE, limits spectral comparison to target spectra with matching precursor m/z to speed up calculations ;; MAPFUN=Function used to align/map peaks between spectra (e.g., joinPeaksNone to disable default mapping when using external similarity functions) ;; FUN=Similarity scoring function (e.g., msentropy_similarity or MsCoreUtils::ndotproduct) ;; queryAssay=Character, name of the assay to use when the query is a QFeatures object ;; iterativeRandomization=Logical, if TRUE, randomizes input rows iteratively to fit standard mix constraints in createStandardMixes()
- alternatives: Spectra::compareSpectra()=Can be used directly for matching fragment spectra, but MetaboAnnotation's matchSpectra() is preferred for end-users as it simplifies handling of potential one-to-many or one-to-none matching results via MatchedSpectra ;; xcms=Functions like chromPeaksSpectra() or featureSpectra() can be used to extract query MS2 spectra before passing them to matchSpectra() ;; msentropy=The msentropy_similarity() function can be used as an alternative similarity function within CompareSpectraParam
- when_to_use: Use when annotating untargeted metabolomics or lipidomics features (m/z, retention times, or MS2 spectra) against reference databases (like LipidMaps, MassBank, or custom CompDb databases) or matching LC-MS features to LC-MS/MS fragment spectra.
- pitfalls: SQL-based backends (e.g., MsBackendCompDb, MsBackendSql) do not support parallel processing because database connections cannot be shared across processes ;; When using alternative similarity functions like msentropy_similarity(), the default peak mapping must be disabled by setting MAPFUN = joinPeaksNone to avoid double-mapping ;; Extracting columns (like feature_id) using $ from a Matched object before subsetting to matched features can return values for unmatched features, leading to misalignment if not handled carefully (use whichQuery() or queryIndex() to map correctly) ;; Memory demand is higher when converting backends to MsBackendMemory for performance gains

workflows.name: match_values
workflows.intent: Match experimental LC-MS features (m/z and retention times) from data.frames, SummarizedExperiment, or QFeatures objects against a reference database of exact masses or m/z values.
input: ms1_features.txt (tab-delimited text file containing feature_id, mz, and rtime)
LipidMaps_CompDB.txt (tab-delimited text file containing reference compound headgroup, name, exactmass, and formula)
workflows.stages: 1. Load query and target datasets ;; 2. Define matching parameters using Mass2MzParam or Mass2MzRtParam ;; 3. Perform matching using matchValues() ;; 4. Inspect and extract matches using matchedData(), whichQuery(), and whichTarget()
workflows.code:
ms1_features <- read.table(system.file("extdata", "MS1_example.txt", package = "MetaboAnnotation"), header = TRUE, sep = "\t")
target_df <- read.table(system.file("extdata", "LipidMaps_CompDB.txt", package = "MetaboAnnotation"), header = TRUE, sep = "\t")
parm <- Mass2MzParam(adducts = c("[M+H]+", "[M+Na]+"), tolerance = 0.005, ppm = 0)
matched_features <- matchValues(ms1_features[1:100, ], target_df, parm)
head(query(matched_features))
head(target(matched_features))
whichQuery(matched_features)
whichTarget(matched_features)
colnames(matched_features)
matchedData(matched_features)
matched_features$target_name
ms1_subset <- ms1_features[1:100, ]
set.seed(123)
target_df$rtime <- sample(ms1_subset$rtime, nrow(target_df), replace = TRUE) + 2
parm <- Mass2MzRtParam(adducts = c("[M+H]+", "[M+Na]+"), tolerance = 0.005, ppm = 0, toleranceRt = 10)
matched_features <- matchValues(ms1_subset, target_df, param = parm, rtColname = "rtime")
matchedData(matched_features)[whichQuery(matched_features), ]
library(SummarizedExperiment)
se <- SummarizedExperiment(assays = matrix(rnorm(nrow(ms1_features) * 4), ncol = 4, dimnames = list(NULL, c("A", "B", "C", "D"))), rowData = ms1_features)
parm <- Mass2MzParam(adducts = c("[M+H]+", "[M+Na]+"), tolerance = 0.005, ppm = 0)
matched_features <- matchValues(se, target_df, param = parm)
colnames(matched_features)
matchedData(matched_features)
matched_sub <- matched_features[whichQuery(matched_features)]
MetaboAnnotation::query(matched_sub)
library(QFeatures)
qf <- QFeatures(list(features = se))
matched_qf <- matchValues(qf, target_df, param = parm, queryAssay = "features")
colnames(matched_qf)
matchedData(matched_qf)

workflows.name: match_spectra
workflows.intent: Match experimental MS2 spectra against a reference spectral library (such as MassBank or a custom Spectra object).
input: PestMix1_DDA.mzML (raw LC-MS/MS data file containing experimental MS2 spectra)
minimb.RData (RData file containing a subset of MassBank reference spectra)
workflows.stages: 1. Load query and target Spectra objects ;; 2. Define similarity parameters using CompareSpectraParam or MatchForwardReverseParam ;; 3. Perform spectral matching using matchSpectra() ;; 4. Extract, filter, and visualize matches using spectraData() and plotSpectraMirror()
workflows.code:
library(Spectra)
library(MsDataHub)
fl <- MsDataHub::PestMix1_DDA.mzML()
pest_ms2 <- filterMsLevel(Spectra(fl), 2L)
pest_ms2 <- pest_ms2[c(808, 809, 945:955)]
pest_ms2$feature_id <- c("FT001", "FT001", "FT002", "FT003", "FT003", "FT003", "FT004", "FT004", "FT004", "FT005", "FT005", "FT006", "FT006")
pest_ms2$spectrum_id <- paste0("sp_", seq_along(pest_ms2))
load(system.file("extdata", "minimb.RData", package = "MetaboAnnotation"))
csp <- CompareSpectraParam(requirePrecursor = TRUE, ppm = 10, matchedPeaksCount = TRUE)
mtches <- matchSpectra(pest_ms2, minimb, param = csp)
length(pest_ms2)
length(mtches)
mtches[1]
mtches[2]
spectraVariables(mtches)
mtches[2]$target_compound_name
mtches$spectrum_id
mtches$.original_query_index
query(mtches)$.original_query_index
mtches_df <- spectraData(mtches, columns = c("spectrum_id", "feature_id", "score", "target_spectrum_id", "target_compound_name"))
as.data.frame(mtches_df)
plotSpectraMirror(mtches[2])
scale_int <- function(x, ...) {
    x[, "intensity"] <- x[, "intensity"] / max(x[, "intensity"], na.rm = TRUE)
    x
}
mtches <- addProcessing(mtches, scale_int)
plotSpectraMirror(mtches[2])
mp <- MatchForwardReverseParam(requirePrecursor = TRUE, ppm = 10)
mtches <- matchSpectra(pest_ms2, minimb, param = mp)
as.data.frame(spectraData(mtches, c("spectrum_id", "target_spectrum_id", "target_compound_name", "score", "reverse_score", "presence_ratio")))
select_top_match <- function(x) {
    which.max(x)
}
csp2 <- CompareSpectraParam(ppm = 10, requirePrecursor = FALSE, THRESHFUN = select_top_match)
mtches <- matchSpectra(pest_ms2, minimb, param = csp2)
res <- spectraData(mtches, columns = c("spectrum_id", "target_spectrum_id", "target_compound_name", "score"))
as.data.frame(res)
library(msentropy)
csp <- CompareSpectraParam(requirePrecursor = TRUE, ppm = 10, matchedPeaksCount = TRUE, MAPFUN = joinPeaksNone, FUN = msentropy_similarity, ms2_tolerance_in_ppm = 10, ms2_tolerance_in_da = -1)
mtches <- matchSpectra(pest_ms2, minimb, param = csp)
mbank <- MassBankSource("2022.06")
res <- matchSpectra(pest_ms2, mbank, param = CompareSpectraParam(requirePrecursor = TRUE, ppm = 10))
target(res)
matchedData(res)$target_name

workflows.name: create_standard_mixes
workflows.intent: Group standard compounds into mixes such that compounds in the same mix have a minimum m/z difference to avoid overlapping signals during LC-MS runs.
input: Standard_list_example.txt (tab-delimited text file containing standard compound names and chemical formulas)
workflows.stages: 1. Load standard compound list ;; 2. Calculate exact masses and theoretical m/z values for desired adducts ;; 3. Group compounds into mixes using createStandardMixes() ;; 4. Export designed mixes to a text file
workflows.code:
library(MetaboCoreUtils)
standard <- read.table(system.file("extdata", "Standard_list_example.txt", package = "MetaboAnnotation"), header = TRUE, sep = "\t", quote = "")
standard$mass <- calculateMass(standard$formula)
standard_charged <- mass2mz(standard$mass, adduct = c("[M+H]+", "[M+Na]+"))
rownames(standard_charged) <- standard[ , 1]
if (!is.matrix(standard_charged))
    standard_charged <- as.matrix(standard_charged, drop = FALSE)
group_no_randomization <- createStandardMixes(standard_charged[1:20,])
table(group_no_randomization$group)
group_no_randomization <- createStandardMixes(standard_charged)
table(group_no_randomization$group)
group_with_ramdomization <- createStandardMixes(standard_charged, iterativeRandomization = TRUE)
table(group_with_ramdomization$group)
set.seed(123)
group_with_ramdomization <- createStandardMixes(standard_charged, max_nstd = 15, min_nstd = 10, min_diff = 2, iterativeRandomization = TRUE)
table(group_with_ramdomization$group)
write.table(group_with_ramdomization, file = "standard_mixes.txt", sep = "\t", quote = FALSE)
